name: Pro Sports Transactions Archive (prosportstransactions.com)
derived_from: newspaper transaction columns, transcribed by hand over twenty years
_status: CHARACTERISED, NOT FETCHED. Nothing has been taken from this source.

ACCESS.browser: Cloudflare interstitial - 'Performing security verification ... protect against malicious bots'
ACCESS.what_I_did: stopped. Bypassing or completing bot-detection is not something this project does, and no amount of the data being useful changes that. The structure below came from the Wayback CDX index, which is a different service and required no evasion.
ACCESS.what_would_unblock_it: Ryan visiting the site himself, or an export/API if the compiler offers one. It is one person's twenty-year compilation; asking is the right route anyway.

RANKING.why: a hand compilation of newspaper transaction columns. Good, and not a document. It is one transcriber's reading of a contemporaneous report.
RANKING.hard_rule: where it disagrees with a court record, a contract, or a club's own document, IT LOSES. It may corroborate a primary source and may stand alone where nothing primary exists, but it never outranks one.

structure_from_CDX._what_that_shows: basketball was compiled first and is far deeper. Football is a sixth of it by archived URL count - which measures what the Wayback crawler saw, not what the database holds.
structure_from_CDX._it_is_a_QUERY_INTERFACE: there are no per-player pages to enumerate. Everything arrives through SearchResults.php with parameters, paginated in blocks of 25 (`start`).

categories.PlayerMovementChkBx: trades, signings, waivings, releases - the dominant use, 785 of the archived queries
categories.NBADLChkBx: a BASKETBALL field appearing in football URLs - the form is shared across sports, so the checkbox list is not evidence of what the football data contains

HOW_FAR_BACK_FOOTBALL_GOES.answer: UNKNOWN. This is the question that decides whether the source is useful for the historical eras, and the CDX index cannot answer it.
HOW_FAR_BACK_FOOTBALL_GOES.the_tempting_wrong_answer: archived queries carry BeginDate values from 1920 to 2021. That is what people TYPED INTO A FORM, not what the database returned. Reading it as coverage would be inferring content from a request - the same error as counting headings and inferring tables (report 38).
HOW_FAR_BACK_FOOTBALL_GOES.how_to_settle_it: one search on the live site with a 1920s date range

why_it_matters.the_gap_it_fills: report 37 found Pro Football Archives' transactions section gone from the live site - 3,945 pages, Wayback-only, out of reach. This is the same category from a source that still exists.
why_it_matters.injuries: nothing in the archive records why a career stopped or why a man missed a season. Every bio currently ends by simply stopping.
why_it_matters.movement: the archive knows a man was at Cleveland in 1953 and Ottawa in 1954. It does not know whether he jumped, was traded, or was waived.
